anomalies.observed: On the CAN BUS sheet, D10 (next to transceiver U11) and D9 (next to transceiver U10) are drawn as optocouplers/photocouplers (input LED + output phototransistor symbol with 'Input 1/Input 2/Output' pins), wired across the CAN0_P/CAN0_N and CAN1_P/CAN1_N differential pairs. No CDSOT23-SM712 (or any SM712-type) TVS diode array appears anywhere on the CAN lines; the only TVS arrays on the board are the TPD4E1U06DCKR parts on the Ethernet transformer.
anomalies.expected: The specification's component table states D9 and D10 are 'CDSOT23-SM712 TVS diode arrays on CAN0_P/N, CAN1_P/N' for 'CAN bus transient/ESD protection', and notes 'the netlist's CDSOT23-SM712 matches this documented choice'. The intended parts are two-diode TVS arrays to ground, not optocouplers.

evidence.quote: D9, D10 — CDSOT23-SM712 TVS diode arrays on CAN0_P/N, CAN1_P/N | CAN bus transient/ESD protection | ... the netlist's CDSOT23-SM712 matches this documented choice.

CAN BUS sheet: U11 (MCP2515 transceiver) with D10 drawn as an optocoupler (Input 1/Input 2/Output + phototransistor) tied across CAN0_P/CAN0_N; U10 with D9 likewise across CAN1_P/CAN1_N. No SM712 part present on the CAN lines.

anomalies.impact: The documented CAN transient/ESD protection is absent on the field M12 CAN connectors (J2/J13), leaving the buses unprotected. Worse, an optocoupler LED placed directly across a CAN differential pair clamps the dominant differential voltage (~1.2 V vs the ~2 V required), so the CAN0/CAN1 buses would likely fail to communicate.

parsed.summary: Most of the board matches the spec (16 MHz crystals on U8/U9, SN74LVC1G07 e-stop sinks, LTC4412+P-MOS USB path, ISL54222AIUZ mux, WS2812B chain), but the two CAN bus protection devices D9/D10 are drawn as optocouplers instead of the specified CDSOT23-SM712 TVS arrays, removing the documented ESD/transient protection and likely shorting/clamping the CAN differential pairs.
